claim: Cholesterol extraction from pancreatic beta cells disrupts the internalisation, clustering, and cAMP responses of the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R).
source: Cholesterol extraction from pancreatic beta cells has previously been shown to disrupt the internalisation, clustering, and cAMP responses of the glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R), a class B1 GPCR with key roles in the control of blood glucose levels via the potentiation of insulin secretion in beta cells and weight reduction via the modulation of brain appetite control centres.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work (Buenaventura et al., 2019) mentioned in the manuscript.

claim: A high cholesterol diet has a detrimental effect on GLP-1R-dependent glucoregulation in vivo.

evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from IPGTTs in mice fed high cholesterol diet shown in Figure 1A-C.

claim: Reduction in cholesterol synthesis using simvastatin improves GLP-1R function in pancreatic islets.
source: the improvement in GLP-1R function that a reduction in cholesterol synthesis using simvastatin exerts in pancreatic islets
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing increased exendin-4-induced cAMP and insulin secretion in simvastatin-treated islets (Figure 1G-I).

claim: Sites of cholesterol high occupancy and residence time on active vs inactive GLP-1Rs were identified using coarse-grained molecular dynamics (cgMD) simulations.

evidence: This claim is supported by computational data from cgMD simulations shown in Figure 2.

claim: The V229A mutation in GLP-1R affects receptor-cholesterol interactions, plasma membrane behaviours, clustering, trafficking and signalling in INS-1 832/3 rat pancreatic beta cells and primary mouse islets.

evidence: This claim is supported by multiple experimental assays shown in Figures 3-8.

claim: The V229A mutant receptor has an improved insulin secretion profile.

evidence: This claim is supported by insulin secretion data in INS-1 832/3 cells and primary islets shown in Figure 8C-D and 8H-I.
